faqs.question: What should I write on a Diwali gift tag?
faqs.answer: One line that names the person and one specific thing about them, 25–40 characters if you are writing by hand on a 5 × 3 cm tag. "For Dadi, who taught me to roll a wick." is 39 characters, spaces included.

faqs.question: How many characters fit on a small gift tag?
faqs.answer: Roughly 25–40 handwritten characters on a 5 × 3 cm tag, by our estimate of about 4 mm per character and 6 mm between lines. Leave room for the sign-off: "—Riya" takes 5 characters.

faqs.question: What do I write on a hamper card for Diwali?
faqs.answer: Two short sentences, the first pointing at what is inside. For a plant, "This one outlasts the rangoli. Water it, and think of us." is 57 characters; keep a visiting-card-size card under about 100.

faqs.question: What goes on a mithai box I made at home?
faqs.answer: What it is, the date you made it, and one light line, such as "Kaju katli from our kitchen, made 27 Oct. Eat the corner pieces first." (70 characters). The date helps a family that receives several boxes on the same evening.

faqs.question: What can a company print on Diwali gifts for its staff?
faqs.answer: One thank-you and one wish, signed by the company by name, such as "Thank you for the year you gave us. Shubh Deepavali from all at Kavya Textiles." (79 characters). Leave out offers and discount codes.

faqs.question: Which line works for clients who may not celebrate Diwali?
faqs.answer: "Light, rest and a calm year-end to you and yours." (49 characters) suits a mixed list. Print it neatly: in a 2019 University of Nevada, Reno study, neat presentation helped gifts that came from acquaintances.

faqs.question: Can I write the tag in Hindi?
faqs.answer: Yes. "मीठा कम, प्यार ज़्यादा। शुभ दीपावली" (Meetha kam, pyaar zyaada. Shubh Deepavali: "Less sugar, more love") shows 21 visible characters but 35 Unicode code points, so it fits a small tag by hand but may fill an online message box sooner.

faqs.question: Does Amazon.in print a gift message on Diwali orders?
faqs.answer: Its gift-wrap help page, checked on 22 October 2026, says wrapped orders carry a printed card with your message on top of the package, from ₹30 for eligible items fulfilled by Amazon. Third-party sellers set their own gift options.

faqs.question: Should the tag for my house help say something different?
faqs.answer: Name what they did instead of only wishing them well, as in "Sunita didi, thank you for this whole year." (43 characters). A 2025 study found indebtedness predicted who got thank-you gifts, so a specific reason keeps the gift personal.

faqs.question: What can I send if I cannot hand the gift over this Diwali?
faqs.answer: SubhSandesh's interactive Diwali card opens on a diya at their door carrying your tag, so a short line from this post fits it, and it travels as a private link with no app needed. For a partner, the hand-tied digital bouquet page is the alternative.

faqs.question: When is Diwali 2027?
faqs.answer: Lakshmi Puja is on Friday 29 October 2027, with Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October and Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October. Date a homemade box and any "29th" line to match.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Gift Message Lines for Tags, Hampers and Sweet Boxes, Counted to the Character

A good Diwali gift message is one line: 25–45 characters on a small tag, up to about 100 on a hamper card, with the recipient's name inside that count. That is far shorter than people write when they have room. On SubhSandesh's miss-you pages the median letter runs 88 words (n = 214, measured September 2026), which is more than ten small tags' worth.

Tags get written late, too: our only festival timing data, from Raksha Bandhan 2026, shows 49.4% of rakhi pages made on the day itself (n = 89). So the 27 lines below for Diwali on 29 October 2027 are ready to copy, sorted by recipient and by what is in the box, each with an exact character count including spaces.

## How long should a Diwali gift message be for each tag size?

The space decides the length, not the relationship. The estimates assume about 4 mm per handwritten character and 6 mm between lines; that is our arithmetic, not a standard, so test one tag first.

| Where the line goes | Typical size (EST) | Characters that fit (EST) | Example from this post | Its count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small swing tag on a bag or box | about 5 × 3 cm | 25–40, handwritten | "For the loudest laugh in our lane." | 34 |
| Hamper card, visiting-card size | about 9 × 5.5 cm | 60–100, handwritten | "This one outlasts the rangoli. Water it, and think of us." | 57 |
| Card tucked under a sweet-box lid | about 7 × 7 cm | 60–90, handwritten | "Kaju katli from our kitchen, made 27 Oct. Eat the corner pieces first." | 70 |
| Insert card in an office gift pack | A6, 14.8 × 10.5 cm | 80–150, printed | "Thank you for the year you gave us. Shubh Deepavali from all at Kavya Textiles." | 79 |

Budget the sign-off before you choose the line. "—Riya" takes 5 characters and "Love, the Mehtas" takes 16, which is a third of a small tag.

## Diwali gift tag messages under 45 characters, by recipient

A tag carries one idea, ideally something only the two of you know: a habit, a flat number, last year's joke. All nine lines below fit a 5 × 3 cm tag.

- **Parents:** "Ma, Papa: the first diya was always yours." (42)
- **A grandmother:** "For Dadi, who taught me to roll a wick." (39)
- **An elder brother:** "Bhaiya, this one was not on sale. Promise." (42)
- **A friend you will see on the day:** "Open after the aarti, not before. —Riya" (39)
- **The neighbours:** "From flat 302, with light. Shubh Deepavali!" (43)
- **A child:** "For the loudest laugh in our lane." (34)
- **A partner:** "Our first Diwali in this flat. Yours, A." (40)
- **The didi who works in your home:** "Sunita didi, thank you for this whole year." (43)
- **In-laws:** "Mummy ji, Papa ji: Shubh Deepavali." (35)

Swap in your own names and details. A line that names the person plus one specific thing reads as written for them, even at 34 characters.

## Diwali hamper messages matched to what is inside

A hamper card has room for two short sentences, so let the first point at the contents. Saying why you chose the almonds or the diyas does what a long greeting cannot, in under 90 characters.

- **Dry fruits:** "Almonds for the memory you say you've lost, cashews for the evenings. Love, the Mehtas." (87)
- **Diyas and candles:** "Twelve diyas, one for each month we called too little. Light them on the 29th." (78)
- **A puja thali set:** "A new thali for your Lakshmi Puja. Keep the old one; it has stories." (68)
- **Chocolates instead of mithai:** "Not mithai, we know. The mithai arrives in person on Bhai Dooj." (63)
- **A plant:** "This one outlasts the rangoli. Water it, and think of us." (57)
- **Tea:** "Assam for slow mornings, masala chai for the guests who never leave." (68)

The "29th" line is written for Lakshmi Puja 2027, so change the date in any other year. The chocolate line's promise comes due on Bhai Dooj, Sunday 31 October 2027.

## What to write on a box of Diwali sweets

Sweet boxes travel furthest, so the lid card is often read by people other than the one you meant. Write for the whole household, in 40–70 characters.

- **A homemade box:** "Kaju katli from our kitchen, made 27 Oct. Eat the corner pieces first." (70)
- **The building's neighbours:** "Sweet things for sweet neighbours. From 4B." (43)
- **A child's own box:** "Arjun gets the first piece. Then the rest. Then the box." (56)
- **A parent with diabetes:** "No sugar, as ordered by your doctor. All the love, as ordered by us." (68)
- **The office floor:** "From everyone at desk 14: Shubh Deepavali." (42)

On a homemade box, the date it was made is the most useful thing on the card. A family that receives six boxes on the same evening can then decide which to open first; 27 October 2027 is Dhanteras.

## Corporate Diwali gift pack messages for staff, clients and vendors

An office insert is usually printed, so tone matters more than length. Keep to one thank-you and one wish; a discount code inside a gift reads like an invoice.

- **Employees:** "Thank you for the year you gave us. Shubh Deepavali from all at Kavya Textiles." (79)
- **Clients:** "Grateful for your trust this year. May your home and office both stay well lit." (79)
- **Vendors and delivery partners:** "For the team that never missed a dispatch. Happy Diwali, and rest well." (71)
- **A list of mixed faiths:** "Light, rest and a calm year-end to you and yours." (49)

Presentation counts for more with these people than with friends. In a 2019 study summarised by the [University of Nevada, Reno](https://www.unr.edu/nevada-today/news/2019/gift-wrapping), Jessica and Brett Rixom found that neat wrapping raised expectations of a friend's gift and lowered liking for it, while a neatly wrapped gift from an acquaintance drew more favourable attitudes. A client is an acquaintance, so print the card cleanly and save the scrawl for your cousins.

## Hindi and Hinglish gift tag lines, and why Devanagari counts differently

A Hindi line can look shorter than its count. Unicode's text segmentation standard, [UAX #29](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/) (version 18.0.0, dated 1 September 2026), separates code points from "user-perceived characters" and gives the Devanagari syllable क्षि as one perceived character built from four code points.

- "दीयों जैसी रोशन रहे आपकी हर शाम" (*Diyon jaisi roshan rahe aapki har shaam*: "May your every evening glow like the diyas.") 31 code points, 22 visible characters
- "मीठा कम, प्यार ज़्यादा। शुभ दीपावली" (*Meetha kam, pyaar zyaada. Shubh Deepavali*: "Less sugar, more love. Happy Deepavali.") 35 code points, 21 visible characters
- "Ghar ki mithai, ghar jaisa pyaar. Happy Diwali!" ("Sweets from home, love like home.") 47 characters

On a handwritten tag, only the visible count matters. An online gift-message box may count code points, so type a Hindi line into the box before trimming anything.

## Why a thank-you gift needs a named reason on its tag

Many Diwali gifts are thank-yous: to the didi, the watchman, the driver, a child's tutor. [Oishi and colleagues](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12106001) (*Applied Psychology: Health and Well-Being*, June 2025; 1,008 participants across three studies) found that indebtedness, not gratitude, fondness or respect, predicted who received a thank-you gift.

Our reading, not theirs: a gift driven by a sense of debt can feel like settling an account. A tag that names what the person actually did, such as "for this whole year" or "for every 6 a.m. gate", turns it back into thanks.

## Adding a gift message to an online Diwali order

When a shop prints the line for you, the handwriting is gone, so the words carry everything. [Amazon.in's gift-wrap help page](https://www.amazon.in/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=G6RLNNT974EPS5US), checked on 22 October 2026, says wrapped orders include a printed card with your gift message on top of the package, and quotes wrapping at ₹30 for eligible items fulfilled by Amazon, with prices varying by size and shape.

Third-party sellers choose their own gift options, so the message box may not appear at all. Write the line before checkout and sign it, because a printed card has no handwriting to tell them who sent it.

## Where SubhSandesh's Diwali page fits next to a gift

Some gifts cannot be handed over, such as one for a parent in another city. The first thing the recipient meets on [SubhSandesh's interactive Diwali card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) is a diya at their door carrying your tag, so one of the short lines above fits it as written, and the last is a mithai box with your Shubh Deepavali card inside.

Between those, the diya wishes, the liffafa letter and up to six photos are yours to fill (the AI can draft from a few lines about you both), in a love, family or friend version. Building one takes roughly five minutes; the link needs no app or login, and since 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone (September 2026), check it on one first.

For a partner far away, the [hand-tied digital bouquet](https://subhsandesh.in/bouquet-gf) is the closer match to flowers with a card. It is a romantic page, not a Diwali one, so keep it for the person you would have sent roses to.

## When a handwritten tag beats a link

A link does not replace a gift you can hand over. A grandparent without a smartphone, the neighbour across the corridor, the didi who works in your home: for them a box and a 35-character tag in your own handwriting do more than any page.

The page also loses on keeping. A tag can stay tied to a thali for years, while a link depends on someone opening it again, even with the final card downloadable at 1080 × 1920 pixels. If you can do only one, give the box and write the tag.

## Sources

- Rixom, J., Mas, E. and Rixom, B., "Presentation matters: The effect of wrapping neatness on gift attitudes", summarised by the [University of Nevada, Reno](https://www.unr.edu/nevada-today/news/2019/gift-wrapping), 9 December 2019.
- Unicode Consortium, [UAX #29: Unicode Text Segmentation](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/), version 18.0.0, 1 September 2026.
- Oishi, S., Lee, M., Koo, M. and Cha, Y., [The psychology of a thank-you gift: Who gives it and why?](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12106001), *Applied Psychology: Health and Well-Being*, June 2025.
- Amazon.in, [Gift Wrap help page](https://www.amazon.in/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=G6RLNNT974EPS5US), checked 22 October 2026.

The domain is far weaker than the gift retailers and wishes sites that rank, the tag-capacity figures are estimates rather than measurements, and there is no Diwali usage data, so expect months, not weeks.
